small_guidance:
- Swap the loop order so IC is the inner-most accumulation and use `tl.dot`: load an `[BLOCK_SP, BLOCK_IC]` tile of x and `[BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_OC]` tile of w per (kd,kh,kw), then `acc += tl.dot(x_tile, w_tile)`. Current code does scalar outer products of shape [128,1]×[1,32] which leaves tensor cores unused.
- Add a `triton.autotune` sweep over `BLOCK_OC∈{32,64}`, `BLOCK_SP∈{64,128,256}`, `BLOCK_IC∈{16,32}`, `num_warps∈{4,8}`, `num_stages∈{2,3,4}`; current 32/128/4w/2s is almost certainly suboptimal for this 16×64×32×64×64 output.
- Hoist `IH*IW`, `OD*OHW`, `OC*KD*KH*KW`, `ID*IH*IW` into local constants once before the kd/kh/kw loops, and precompute per-tile spatial-mask once outside the IC loop so the inner loop is purely loads + dot.
large_guidance:
- Re-cast as a scatter-add (input-stationary) kernel: parallelize over `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)`, load one `[BLOCK_SP, BLOCK_IC]` x tile and the full `[BLOCK_IC, OC, KD*KH*KW]` weight slab, compute the `input × weight` outer product, and atomically scatter into output positions `(id*stride - pad + kd, ...)`. This is the canonical fast ConvTranspose3d formulation and turns the current per-output gather (which does `IC * KD*KH*KW` redundant valid-position checks per output element) into a dense matmul with one scatter per kernel tap.
- Alternatively, do gemm-based im2col but tile over `(N, OC tile=64, OutSpatial tile=128)` with `BLOCK_K=IC=32` as a single `tl.dot`, with the KD*KH*KW loop on the outside writing into the same accumulator; channels-last (NDHWC) input + weight layout will make the K-dim contiguous and let one `tl.dot` per kernel tap saturate the tensor cores.
- Fold the conv bias and the `(2y+b)*y + y` epilogue into the same kernel's store path (already done) but also fuse the bias load once per program rather than re-broadcasting; persist the OC tile across the spatial loop so bias and weight stay in registers/shared memory.
